title: Rome: 1 Cor 11 — I received from the Lord what I delivered; the rest I will set in order
source_text: IX. Nec majorem vim habet alterum testimonium, quod ex eodem capite adversarii desumunt. Apostolus enim, modum expositurus celebrandae Coenae Dominicae, sic sermonem suum orditur, Ego accepi a Domino, quod & tradidi vobis: & tandem concludit his verbis, Cetera quum venero disponam. Ubi primum Bellarminus urget vocem tradidi, quasi faceret aliquid ad traditiones non scriptas. Deinde addit nusquam scriptum inveniri quid Paulus disposuerit. Merito autem Catholicos censere eum non solum disposuisse quae ad ritus & ceremonias pertinebant, sed etiam tradidisse alia graviora, ut de ordinatione Ministrorum, de sacrificio altaris, de aliorum Sacramentorum materia & forma, nec haereticos posse contrarium ostendere.
pass_a_gloss: Nor does the other testimony which the adversaries take from the same chapter have greater force. For the Apostle, about to set forth the manner of celebrating the Lord's Supper, thus begins his speech, I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you: and at length concludes with these words, The rest I will set in order when I come. Where first Bellarmine presses the word I delivered, as if it did something for unwritten traditions. Then he adds that nowhere is it found written what Paul arranged. But that Catholics rightly judge that he arranged not only things which pertained to rites and ceremonies, but also delivered other graver things, as concerning the ordination of Ministers, concerning the sacrifice of the altar, concerning the matter and form of the other Sacraments, and that heretics cannot show the contrary.
pass_b_english: Rome's second 1 Cor 11 text: I received from the Lord what I delivered — the rest when I come.
Bellarmine leans on delivered as if it proved unwritten tradition.
He adds that Paul's later arrangements are nowhere written.
Catholics fill the gap with ordination, altar-sacrifice, and sacrament matter and form.
